Grammatik: eigentlich: Adverb oder Modal: Grammar: eigentlich: adverb or modal particle (Modalpartikel)?
Dasselbe Wort hat zwei ganz verschiedene: The same word has two completely different functions, and the stress decides which. Stressed and usually at the front of the sentence, eigentlich is an adverb and means “in reality, basically” — often followed by a contrast. Unstressed in the middle field (Mittelfeld), it is a modal particle (Modalpartikel) and makes a question more casual or friendlier.
Eigentlich wollte ich nur ein Semester b: Actually, I only wanted to stay for one semester — it turned into three years.
Das ist eigentlich kein Problem, sondern: That is actually not a problem but an opportunity.
Wie lange bist du eigentlich schon hier?: How long have you been here, actually?
Wolltest du nicht eigentlich früher Besc: Weren't you actually going to let me know earlier?
Eigentlich hatte ich mit Heimweh gerechn: Actually, I had expected to be homesick, but I didn't miss anything. Adverb — expectation versus reality
Was machst du eigentlich beruflich?Modal: So what do you do for a living? Modal particle — makes the question less direct
Die Stadt ist eigentlich zu teuer für St: The city is actually too expensive for students. Adverb — “strictly speaking”
Tipp: Als Modalpartikel kann eigentlich: Tip: As a modal particle, eigentlich can never be in position 1. If it is at the front, it is always the adverb.

Die Studie wurde von Hirnforschern durch: The study was carried out by brain researchers.
Die Information wurde durch einen Kolleg: The information was passed on through a colleague.
Der Test wurde von der Uni durch eine On: The data for the test were collected by the university through an online survey.
Das Kurzzeitgedächtnis wird durch Stress: Short-term memory is noticeably impaired by stress. — cause → durch
Die Theorie wurde von einer Forschergrup: The theory was developed by a research group in Leipzig. — agent → von
Viele Inhalte werden durch Wiederholung: A lot of content is stored permanently through repetition. — means → durch
Tipp: Faustregel: Wer handelt bewusst? →: Tip: Rule of thumb: Who acts deliberately? → von. What has an effect without intending to? → durch.

Grammatik: Passiv mit Konjunktiv II der: Grammar: The passive with the past subjunctive II (Konjunktiv II der Vergangenheit)
Um zu sagen, was in der Vergangenheit hä: To say what could or should have been done in the past, you combine the past subjunctive II with the passive. The structure is: hätte + past participle (Partizip II) + werden; with a modal verb, the modal verb in the infinitive is also added at the very end.
wäre + Partizip II + worden: wäre + past participle + worden (would have been …)
